summary.en: Understand what Python does and how it differs from C before you start writing programs.
summary.bn: কোড লেখা শুরুর আগে পাইথনের কাজ আর C-এর সঙ্গে পার্থক্য বুঝে নাও।

notes: These programs target Python 3.12 and use features available in Python 3.10 or later.

sections.title: From instructions to a running program

practice.title: Choose a language for a marks report
practice.statementHtml: A department needs a weekly marks summary from a text file. Explain two reasons to choose Python and one limit.
hints: Think about development time and repeated numeric work.
practice.answerHtml: Python offers text tools and short programs, so you can build the report quickly. Libraries can help with tables. A large loop written in ordinary Python may run slower than compiled C, so measure if processing time matters.

practice.title: Explain the execution path
practice.statementHtml: Describe how CPython runs a saved program. Does interpreted mean that no compilation happens?
practice.answerHtml: CPython reads and compiles source into bytecode. Its interpreter then executes that bytecode. Compilation can therefore happen inside an interpreted implementation. You usually start the script without a separate compiler command.

practice.title: Choose the right major version
practice.statementHtml: A handout uses print without parentheses and asks you to install Python 2. What should you do?
practice.answerHtml: Use Python 3 and find a Python 3 version of the lesson. Python 2 reached end of life in January 2020. Its syntax and some behavior differ, so changing the interpreter alone may not repair old code.

practice.title: Compare a small Python and C workflow
practice.statementHtml: Explain what you normally run after editing a Python script and a C source file. Avoid claiming that either language has only one implementation.
hints: Describe the usual CPython and C compiler workflows.
practice.answerHtml: For Python, save the script and pass its name to a Python interpreter. For C, compile the source and then run the resulting executable. These are common workflows, not rules limiting every possible implementation.

quiz.explanation: Python source describes steps a Python implementation can execute.

quiz.prompt: Which task fits a short Python automation script?
quiz.explanation: Python works well for repeated file and text tasks; it is not limited to notebooks.

quiz.prompt: In the usual CPython workflow, what executes bytecode?
quiz.explanation: CPython compiles source to bytecode and interprets those instructions.

quiz.prompt: Why is “interpreted means never compiled” misleading?
options: Python source is always machine code
CPython compiles source to bytecode before executing it
quiz.explanation: Interpreted and compiled describe execution choices, not exclusive language categories.

quiz.prompt: Which major version should a new learner choose?
quiz.explanation: Python 2 support has ended, and current teaching should target Python 3.

quiz.prompt: What does the 12 in Python 3.12 identify?
quiz.explanation: A version such as 3.12.14 has major, minor and patch components.

quiz.prompt: How are Python names different from declared C int variables?
options: Python names have no spelling rules
A Python name can later refer to another type
quiz.explanation: Python values have types; names are not fixed to a declared type.

quiz.prompt: Why might a team keep a C component in a Python application?
quiz.explanation: C can suit low-level work while Python organises the surrounding application.

quiz.prompt: What is the role of a library in a Python project?
options: A guarantee that any program is safe
quiz.explanation: Libraries supply existing functionality, but the programmer still chooses and checks its use.

quiz.prompt: Which statement about Python release advice stays useful?
options: Check supported releases in the official documentation
quiz.explanation: Release status changes with time; the examples here target Python 3.12.

keyPoints.en: Python is a general-purpose language for many kinds of work.
keyPoints.bn: পাইথন দিয়ে নানা ধরনের প্রোগ্রাম লেখা যায়।

keyPoints.en: CPython translates source into bytecode and then executes it.
keyPoints.bn: CPython সোর্স থেকে বাইটকোড বানিয়ে সেটি চালায়।

keyPoints.en: New programs should use the supported Python 3 family.
keyPoints.bn: নতুন প্রোগ্রামের জন্য সমর্থিত Python 3 ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: Python values have types even when names have no declared type.
keyPoints.bn: নাম ঘোষণা না করলেও পাইথনের প্রতিটি মানের টাইপ থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Choose a language by the work and its constraints.
keyPoints.bn: কাজ আর সীমাবদ্ধতা বুঝে প্রোগ্রামিং ভাষা বেছে নাও।

examQuestions.question: Explain “interpreted language” using CPython as an example.
examQuestions.answerHtml: CPython first compiles source into bytecode, then its interpreter executes the bytecode. Users commonly run scripts directly. Interpreted does not mean that compilation never occurs.

examQuestions.question: Give two uses of Python suitable for a university student and explain each.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An attendance report can count and summarise records. A plotting program can show measured lab results. Both use existing tools to reduce repetitive work.

examQuestions.question: Compare Python and C for a quick reporting tool and for low-level firmware.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Python can shorten reporting code and offers useful libraries. C often suits direct hardware control and tight resource limits. Actual requirements decide the choice; neither language wins every task.
